what_is_checked: first call: guard 0 -> __cxa_guard_acquire -> operator new(0x30) -> the 0x30-byte object is built in the binary store order (+0x08/+0x10/+0x18/+0x28 zeroed, primary vptr +0x00, secondary vptr +0x20) -> instance slot stored -> guard released -> the same pointer is returned
repeat call: the guard fast path returns the same pointer with no second allocation (allocations stays 1)
stub call: the 9-byte forwarder tail-jumps to the factory body, so a stub call constructs on first use and returns the same pointer afterwards
acquire-returns-0: another thread initialized meanwhile; the existing instance is returned with no new allocation
alloc failure: the landing pad runs __cxa_guard_abort then _Unwind_Resume; the guard stays 0, the instance stays None, and a later call retries construction successfully

observations: Both 184-byte bodies reproduce the SAME census source hash (55ccba1f...): they are two instantiations of one source body, the function-local-static singleton getter. Their body hashes differ only through the relocation targets (guard/instance addresses, vtable addresses, landing-pad targets).

The census record's symbol field is _ZN7rocksdb18BytewiseComparatorEv for BOTH copies, with candidate_symbols listing both BytewiseComparator and ReverseBytewiseComparator. The Bytewise/Reverse assignment is therefore pinned independently: 0x61be810 stores vptr 0x64d7038 whose Name slot (+0x70) is 0x61bd720 returning 'leveldb.BytewiseComparator', and CreateFromString calls it from the 26-char 'leveldb.BytewiseComparator' branch (0x61c0451); 0x61be8f0 stores vptr 0x64d7158 whose Name slot is 0x61bd7e0 returning 'rocksdb.ReverseBytewiseComparator', and CreateFromString calls it from the 33-char 'rocksdb.ReverseBytewiseComparator' branch (0x61c0a93).

The guard/instance pairs sit adjacent in .bss in registration order: U64Ts guard 0x65088c8 / instance 0x65088d0 (#5852), reverse guard 0x65088d8 / instance 0x65088e0, bytewise guard 0x65088e8 / instance 0x65088f0. The layout is consistent with three STATIC_AVOID_DESTRUCTION singletons in one translation unit (util/comparator.cc).

Neither body registers an __cxa_atexit handler: the singletons are intentionally leaked (STATIC_AVOID_DESTRUCTION). This differs from the U64Ts Name factory (#5852), which does register its cached std::string for destruction -- the difference is source-level (a Comparator singleton vs a std::string cache), not an omission.

The two stubs are byte-identical (same body hash bcc59137...): each stub ends exactly 0xc9 bytes past its factory's start, so both jmp rel32 displacements are -0xc9. The stubs exist because RegisterBuiltinComparators takes the factories' addresses for its lambdas; direct calls throughout the binary go to the bodies, not the stubs.

The landing pads live in their own 16-byte FDEs (0x61be7fb..0x61be80b for bytewise, 0x61be8d9..0x61be8e9 for reverse): mov rdi,rbx; call __cxa_guard_abort; mov rdi,rbp; call _Unwind_Resume. The third such block, 0x61be9b9..0x61be9c9, belongs to the U64Ts factory (#5852: its landing pad jumps there), not to this packet.

The secondary vtables hold exactly three function slots (thunk D1, thunk D0, Compare copy 2) with offset-to-top -32; the Compare copies 0x61bdd50 / 0x61bdda0 are the second copies reconstructed in #5844. The secondary vptr is stored at object +0x20 as primary + 0xf8.
The primary vtables end at Compare (+0xe0) with a null slot at +0xe8; the +0x98 and +0xd8 slots both hold EqualWithoutTimestamp 0x61bd950 (the derived slot and the Comparator-base slot).
